expectations.text: Recommends splitting the class by responsibility (does NOT endorse keeping all 4 concerns in one file)
expectations.evidence: Title 'Split it'; 'no, keeping it together isn't the right call. I'd split UserService into focused modules' — auth/tokenService.ts, profile/profileRepository.ts, notifications/userEmailer.ts, analytics/userEvents.ts plus thin orchestrator.

expectations.text: Identifies the seams (auth / persistence / email / analytics) as genuinely independent and isolatable
expectations.evidence: 'textbook god object. The four things... are genuinely different concerns with different reasons to change, different dependencies, and different testability profiles' — enumerates auth/tokens, profile CRUD, email, analytics.

expectations.text: Cites the ~300-line ceiling AND/OR multiple-unrelated-concerns as the reason, not blind line count
expectations.evidence: 'A 420-line file with four unrelated responsibilities is harder to reason about than four 80-120 line files'; 'The goal isn't smaller files, it's one reason to change per file' — reasons from concerns, not blind count.

expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'keep everything in one place for the agent' rationale as misapplied to a god object
expectations.evidence: 'Why the one place reasoning doesn't hold up'; 'Claude doesn't read files the way you scroll them... it's noise it has to load'; 'reasonable but it's solving the wrong problem.'
